newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER BIRDIES TO TIE FOR WESTERN OPEN LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER BIRDIES TO TIE FOR WESTERN OPEN LEAD.

text.p: Tiger Woods pumped his fist in delight after sinking a lengthy birdie putt Saturday to tie for the third-round lead at the $2 million Western Open.
"I didn't know if it had enough energy to get there," Woods said of his 18-footer, which trickled in to cap off a four-under-par 68 in perfect conditions on the Cog Hill course.
Woods's finish left the Masters champion tied with fellow-Americans Loren Roberts (66) and Justin Leonard (72) at nine-under 207 with one round to play.
The leading trio stood one stroke ahead of compatriots Steve Lowery (66) and Jim Furyk (67), and New Zealander Frank Nobilo (67).
"I made some big par putts. That was the key today," said Woods, 21, who heads this year's PGA Tour money list with three victories under his belt.
Woods, who has struggled of late, is returning to form after his mini-slump in perfect time for the British Open in a fortnight.

"It's nice to be in contention because it gives you a chance to feel the nerves, the butterflies," he said. "These are things I haven't felt for a while. In golf, the longer you go the more slumps you'll have. It's hard to hit the ball well and putt well for extended periods."

Woods started his round with a bogey at the first hole, where he hooked his drive into the left rough, but his only other dropped shot was at the par-four 13th, where he sank a six-footer to avoid a double bogey.
He compiled six birdies, three of them at par-5s where he got home in two shots and two-putted.
Roberts, meanwhile, did not drop a shot in his 66, equal to the day's lowest round.
"I consider this an almost major," said Roberts, who added that he wants to win this more than any other tournament outside the four majors and the Players Championship.
Second-round leader Leonard did not take advantage of the beautiful conditions, but he had no complaints. "I hung in there, hit enough good shots to keep myself in the tournament," he said.
Nobilo, the only non-American on the leader board, made his move with three birdies in the final eight holes.
"The back nine I played great," he said. "Some of the pins were set pretty tough. I'd rather be in the lead but you just try to make the best of your position."
